newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung hits back at critics of interim chamber.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung hits back at critics of interim chamber.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Wednesday that persistant opposition to Beijing's hand-picked interim lawmaking chamber to be installed upon the handover would only create problems for the territory.
Tung also urged opponents of the provisional legislature to stop criticising the body when talking to Western leaders, adding that their actions were a disservice to Hong Kong.

"I urge those who constantly speak ill against the provisional legislature to the West to stop doing so for the sake of Hong Kong's 6.3 million people," Tung said at a dinner reception attended by a host of top civil servants.

The 60-member interim lawmaking chamber was formed last December under close Chinese supervision, and is poised to replace Hong Kong's elected legislature from July 1 when the British colony reverts to Chinese rule.

Hong Kong's British colonial government has repeatedly said it not would help the body in any way and the territory's pro-democracy camp, particularly the popular Democratic Party, is also virulently opposed to it.
Democratic Party leaders made several lobbying trips abroad last year to urge Western leaders to condemn China's interim chamber as a contravention of Sino-British handover treaties.
But Tung said such actions could only bring harm to Hong Kong.

"There are people in Hong Kong who go to the Western world to put a negative cast on the provisional legislature. It's a complicated issue...and if it's not understood properly, it would mislead people to wrong conclusions," he said.
But when asked later by reporters if he was referring to the Democratic Party, Tung said, "I won't pinpoint anyone. Those people should know who they are."
Tung is scheduled to meet Democratic Party members on Thursday. "I will meet the party tomorrow. I hope to increase communication with them," he said.
